premise.claim: spec.runAfter is mutable, so a user can remove it while the operation is still waiting. reconcileOperationDataFlow then dereferences the nil runAfter (runAfter.Namespace) and panics. Fluid does not enable controller-runtime's RecoverPanic, so the panic kills dataset-controller; the object keeps the same status, so the controller crash-loops.
premise.evidence: On base f432bdc8 the P0 contract specs panic with 'invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference' (results/l1-unit-base-p0-focus.txt, results/l2-envtest-base.txt); on head cc3947c0 they pass and waitingFor.operationComplete is cleared (results/l1-unit-head.txt, results/l2-envtest-head.txt). Replaying the PR's own new tests on base fails 35 Passed | 6 Failed, matching the PR body (results/l1-unit-base-pr-tests-replay.txt).

findings.note: Was a canary on cc3947c0 (spurious write on non-waiting same-name objects). Head 50933d0b added the waiting guard; the canary flipped red, so it was inverted to this contract test asserting the untouched invariant.

Release must record DataOperationWaitingEnded on both release paths (runAfter removed; preceding completed) and only for operations that were waiting. Added in the 50933d0b round; RED on cc3947c0's operations.go.
